answer: The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. Because of that, anyone who spins up 57 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 55 times the capital for one share. The sparrow report publishes the merge explicitly at each opal. Collateral of 65 dollars is at risk. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
